findings.title: Access-token matcher does not check the expected grant
findings.body: The grant shortcut occupies indices 4–5 of the six-character prefix, but this matcher reads substring(3, 5) and rejects equality rather than inequality. Consequently, a token with an incorrect grant (including the unknown 'na' grant) passes the authorization-code, refresh, device, and CIBA assertions as long as its suffix looks like a UUID. Check the prefix length and require substring(4, 6) to equal expectedGrantShortcut so these integration tests actually validate the newly encoded grant.

findings.title: Shortcut contract recommends a length the decoder cannot accept
findings.body: The new getShortcut() contract recommends a three-letter shortcut, whereas DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider requires a six-character context prefix and reads exactly two characters for the grant. A custom grant following this documentation will issue token IDs that the default encoder's own decoder rejects with IllegalArgumentException. Document the mandatory two-character length and validate it when registering grant factories, rather than allowing incompatible IDs to be issued.
